LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FRIENDLY LETTER

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we write friendly letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension
2. write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression
3. enjoy writing friendly letters for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FRIENDLY LETTER
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FRIENDLY LETTER
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression

What this means
In this part you learn to write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Enjoy writing friendly letters for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to enjoy writing friendly letters for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: enjoy writing friendly letters for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can enjoy writing friendly letters for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter to a partner. (skill: write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: enjoy writing friendly letters for communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression.
4. Practise this skill: enjoy writing friendly letters for communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write friendly letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension.
5. Be able to: write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
